cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen, the exchange running level and warm.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in even measure
cells.place: In the middle of becoming what you actually are
cells.ask: Offer the next thing freely, and let yourself take what comes back just as freely — the give and take staying level is what keeps the peace you've built worth keeping.
cells.core: You give what's yours to give and you let what's yours come back — the exchange runs level without you having to check it. Nobody's keeping score, least of all you, and that's exactly why it stays fair. What you are is showing, not because you announced it but because the two-way street is real and people can feel it.
cells.sheetLine: You give and receive in even measure, and it holds.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a reckoning that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: Balancing the books ahead of time
cells.place: At the edge of becoming what you are, but auditing the room instead of standing in it
cells.ask: Let one exchange stay open — hold what's yours without forcing a settlement this week, and let the fairness come back to you on its own timing.
cells.core: You're running the ledger before anything's even owed. You can feel the imbalance coming, so you give ahead of the ask, take ahead of the offer, and adjust everyone's accounts before they've opened them — and the fairness you're chasing keeps receding because you won't let it arrive on its own. You're standing at the threshold of yourself, books in hand, checking whether you deserve to cross.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling a debt nobody's asked you to pay yet.

cells.tense: Past tense — still at a door that has already shut behind you.
cells.place: Somewhere behind the moment you were supposed to be what you are
cells.ask: Bring one small thing to someone and let them bring one back — practice the exchange at the scale you can stand, and let the fairness return by degrees rather than all at once.
cells.core: The exchange stopped and you know it. Something back there made giving or taking feel like a risk, and since then you've been standing outside the give-and-take, watching it happen to other people. The fairness hasn't left you — it's just that the contributing and receiving quit, and what you are got held at the door along with it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped trading, and what you are stopped arriving.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing in.
cells.verb: Keeping fairness in motion between people
cells.place: Already in the middle of becoming what you are, though you'd call it something else
cells.ask: Name one act of yours as generosity out loud — the thing you keep calling just doing your part, said as a gift, and let yourself know it's yours before you decide what to call it next.
cells.core: You've been restoring the balance between people this whole time — through what you hand over, what you let go, what you quietly even out — and you describe it as nothing in particular, just how things go. The exchange is running and you keep it running. What you are is showing through the fairness you keep in motion, and you haven't said so.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the exchange level and call it nothing.
